 WTA Chennai Day 2 Predictions Including Panna Udvardy vs Robin Montgomery 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 After a washout dampened Day 1 at the WTA 250 event in Chennai, all 16 first-round matches are on the schedule for Tuesday. This set of predictions features No. 4 seed Panna Udvardy, while predictions for the rainout matches can be found on LWOT’s website . Who will advance?  
 WTA Chennai Day 2 Predictions 
 Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi vs Katarzyna Kawa  
 Head-to-head: First meeting 
 At 33, Kawa’s having the best season of her career, nearing the Top 100 and a main draw spot in the Australian Open in January. She reached the quarterfinals in Ningbo in October, despite an earlier five-match losing skid over the summer. A 32% win record on hard courts won’t help her chances in this tournament, and she’s playing the home favorite Rajeshwaran Revathi. However, Rajeshwaran Revathi is on a six-match losing streak and fell in straight sets after she received a wildcard last year in Chennai. Look for Kawa to prevail.
 Prediction: Kawa in 2  
 Anastasia Zakharova vs Polina Iatcenko  
 Head-to-head: Iatcenko 1-0  
 In their only meeting, Iatcenko took out Zakharova in a straightforward 6-4 6-2 rout at a 2023 ITF event in Kazakhstan. Since then, Zakharova has had the better WTA Tour success overall, cracking the Top 70 this season and snatching 11 wins this season. Iatcenko has largely played on the ITF Tour, and she sticks to the hard courts — more than 90% of her career ITF matches have taken place on that surface, according to Tennis Abstract . I’ll take Zakharova in an up-and-down match, but this could go either way.   
 Prediction: Zakharova in 2  
 Jodie Burrage vs Vaishnavi Adkar  
 Head-to-head: First meeting 
 Injuries have hurt Burrage over the years, but she got an encouraging win over Rebecca Sramkova in Beijing qualifying earlier in September, the former World No. 33. Adkar is another home favorite from Pune, India, and she’s had some steady results, reaching a WTA 100 final in February. That tournament notably took place on home soil, and I like her chances to take out Burrage in a slight upset, with steady results on home turf.  
 Prediction: Adkar in 3  
 Rada Zolotareva vs Lucrezia Stefanini   
 Head-to-head: First meeting  
 Stefanini is at No. 117 in the world, another player eyeing a big run to elevate herself into the Australian Open main draw cutoff. Zolotareva went on an eight-match winning streak in June on ITF clay courts, but hasn’t been very active on the WTA Tour since then. Stefanini’s distinct double-handed groundstrokes on both the forehand and backhand should also frustrate a less experienced player at a bigger tournament. Look for the Italian to reach the second round.  
 Prediction: Stefanini in 2  
 Panna Udvardy vs Robin Montgomery  
 Head-to-head: First meeting 
 While Montgomery caught some eyes in the summer after big grass court events, the American’s form has been stifled, as she’s aiming for a first WTA Tour win since June. Udvardy holds an 18-21 record on the WTA Tour this year, in her first full season in the big leagues, and her quick movement and topspin should help her against an offensive player like Montgomery.    
 Prediction: Udvardy in 2
